description: Scenario tests for profile-optimization. A run passes only when every item in 'expect' is satisfied. Written before the skill body (test-first).

evals.name: happy-path-profile
evals.input: Optimize my Instagram profile — I'm a solo founder building a SaaS social scheduler.
expect: reads brand-profile, voice, audience, and social-strategy first
applies the 3-second clarity test (who you help, what you offer, why follow) above the fold
uses the searchable name field for a niche keyword, not just the name
writes a who/what/why bio with a clear CTA within the platform's character limit
matches the link to the current goal and specs pinned posts + highlights
delivers a ready-to-apply spec and frames itself as advisory (doesn't claim to edit the profile via WoopSocial)

evals.name: clarity-over-clever-pushback
evals.input: My bio is 'Dream big ✨ | coffee lover ☕ | living my best life 🌴' — polish it up.
expect: pushes back that the bio is vague and doesn't say who it helps, what it does, or why to follow
rewrites it for clarity first (who/what/why) while keeping personality and voice
explains a visitor decides in seconds and confusion loses the follow

evals.name: use-searchable-fields
evals.input: For the name field I'll just put my name, and on LinkedIn my headline is just 'Founder'.
expect: explains the Instagram name field is searchable/indexed and the LinkedIn headline is prime SEO real estate
recommends adding a niche keyword (what you do / who you help), not just the name or title
gives a concrete example like 'Name | what they do'

evals.name: link-cta-match
evals.input: I have one Linktree with 15 links and a 'link in bio' CTA. Good enough?
expect: advises matching the link to the current goal/CTA rather than a cluttered hub of 15 links
recommends a single clear destination (or a tidy hub leading with the priority action) and a specific reason to click
ties the link choice to the strategy's primary goal

evals.name: niche-not-everyone
evals.input: I want my profile to appeal to everyone so I get the most followers.
expect: pushes back that a profile for everyone converts no one
recommends a specific niche/positioning so the right visitor instantly self-identifies
ties this to clarity and the 3-second test

evals.name: banner-brief-not-stock
evals.input: For my LinkedIn banner I'll just use a generic stock photo of a city.
expect: treats the banner/header as prime real estate that should carry a value prop, proof, or CTA
provides a banner brief (what it should communicate visually) rather than a generic image
keeps it on-brand

evals.name: advisory-not-bridge
evals.input: Just update my bio and profile picture directly.
expect: clarifies it can't edit profile fields via WoopSocial (which publishes posts/media, not profile changes)
produces a ready-to-paste spec for the user to apply in each app
does not claim to have made the change

evals.name: new-account-no-proof-and-voice
evals.input: Write my bio but I'm brand new with no followers, results, or testimonials.
evals.context: voice.md bans exclamation marks and hype words.
expect: uses clarity, specificity, and a sharp niche instead of fabricated proof or vanity metrics
does not invent fake numbers, clients, or testimonials
stays on-voice (no exclamation marks or hype words)

evals.name: no-analytics-claims
evals.input: Which bio version performs best for us?
expect: does not claim WoopSocial provides profile analytics
points to native profile insights the user pulls (profile visits, link taps, follows) or qualitative review (does it pass the 3-second test)
frames bio testing as something to observe, not data it can supply
